newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up 2 pct on banks' stock reform.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up 2 pct on banks' stock reform.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended sharply higher on Thursday on hopes that an easing of rules governing banks' shareholdings would draw new capital into the market.
Finance Minister Paul Chiu said after Wednesday's close that Taipei would allow banks to hold 20 percent of their net asset value in stocks, up from 15 percent, effective in July.
The relaxation was expected to bring in additional T$47 billion in the market by banks, experts calculated.
The index rocketed as high as 8,392.96, then settled for a closing gain of 163.68 points or 2.00 percent at 8,367.57.
Turnover was a very heavy T$181.4 billion.
"This shows the government is still adopting a bullish attitude even after recent stock market rallies, thus encouraging investors," said National Securities international sales chief Oliver Fang.
The most heavily weighted financials surged 2.37 percent as brokers said the ministry plan would benefit banks, giving them more flexibility to manage their funds.
Taitung Business Bank surged T$2.4 to T$51.5.
Electronics, after Wednesday's downward correction, emerged again to lead the upward momentum, rising 3.74 percent.
Chipmaker United Microelectronics rose the daily seven percent limit to T$57.5. Computer giant Acer gained T$1.5 to T$71.5.
"Many people have said electronics were overheating, but in the domestic market the strong one is always strong," said Golden Securities research head Albert Lin.
Paper shares rose 3.72 percent on hopes of second quarter pulp price hikes, with Taiwan Pulp limit up to T$34. Brokers said share prices would rise on rising paper demand.
The market is closed on Friday and Saturday for holidays. Brokers said they expect a firming 8,250-8,500 range next week.
